newsitem.title: INDIA: India seeks joint venture partner for Neelam field.
newsitem.headline: India seeks joint venture partner for Neelam field.

text.p: The Indian government is considering a proposal by state-run Oil and Natural Gas Corp (ONGC) to set up a joint venture to develop the Neelam oilfields in its Bombay High offshore field, a senior Petroleum Ministry official said on Tuesday.
"This is a proposal which has been approved by the ONGC board and it has come to us," Petroleum Secretary Vijay Kelkar told reporters on the sidelines of an oil and gas conference in the capital.
Kelkar said ONGC had proposed setting up a joint venture company with a foreign partner to improve recovery and enhance yields from the Neelam oilfields.
He gave no details regarding ONGC's partner in the venture.
The Neelam fields currently produce 2.5 million to three million tonnes of oil annually. Kelkar did not say what annual production was likely to be after formation of the joint venture.
He said the proposal pertained only to the Neelam fields.
"But if the pattern is successful, it will be extended to other oilfields, not only at Bombay High, but all over the country," he said.

Speaking at the two-day conference attended by more than 250 delegates from India and abroad, Kelkar said the federal government was looking at ways to restructure ONGC to help it exploit new reserves and improve its performance.
The government was also planning to set up a gas regulatory body.
